held.label: security
held.title: Artifact pinning can be bypassed
held.reason: Confirmed in code. _read_artifact resolves the path under the evidence root via _resolve, then takes the tracked-at-head_sha branch through _git/_git_bytes, which carry -C _ROOTS['git'] — the SHA root. With the two roots split and the path present in both trees, the returned bytes are the SHA repo's blob and the evidence-root file's artifacts[] sha256 pin is never evaluated for that path.
corrections_to_the_report: The bytes are not unpinned — they are pinned to an immutable commit, in the wrong repo. The defect is that the manifest's own declared pin for that path goes unchecked, so a manifest naming one digest can pass while the verifier reads different bytes.
Reachability is broader than a name collision: in a self-chain, where --git-dir names a second clone of the same repo, every evidence path collides by construction.
held.contradicts: runtime/scripts/verify.py:2100-2102 — the --evidence-root help asserts 'Cross-repo evidence is never tracked at head_sha, so it passes only on its artifacts[] sha256 pin'. That stated invariant does not hold.
held.status: HELD — not fixed; answered in thread https://github.com/ravidsrk/orca-fleet/pull/485#discussion_r4056476809

held.title: Symbol check uses wrong repository
held.reason: Confirmed in code. check_symbol_on_base calls _run(['git','grep','-l','-e',symbol,f'origin/{base}']) directly, bypassing the root-aware _git helper, so the grep runs in the process cwd regardless of --git-dir. The adjacent check_base_ancestry at :1711 resolves the same origin/<base> ref through _git. An audit of the remaining git call sites shows the others are deliberate: :199 is documented as intentionally cwd-bound so --git-dir cannot move the #267 evidence bound, :1390 and :1408 pass -C top from the root-aware _toplevel(), and :2043 is the root validator. :1720 is the only unexplained one.
held.narrowing: The --git-dir help at :2087-2094 enumerates the legs it re-roots and the symbol grep is not among them, so this is arguably out-of-scope-by-documentation rather than a broken promise; it is still wrong for a chained run, since check 8 asks whether the change is real on base and base lives in the SHA repo. Impact is bounded by the check being best-effort, but it still emits a failure line.
